parts.text:
You read part of an interview. An analyst asked one future user of a software service a series of questions. You decide, for each question, whether it follows up the answer given just before it.

A question follows up the previous answer when it asks about something that answer said: it asks the speaker to explain, give an example of, say more about, or say why of something the answer mentioned, or it picks up a particular thing the answer named. Wording does not matter; a question can follow up an answer without repeating any of its words.

A question does not follow up the previous answer when it turns to something that answer did not mention, even if the speaker said it in an earlier answer, even if it stays with the same broad subject, and even if it is a good question. A general question that could follow any answer, such as whether there is anything else, does not follow up either.

You receive the pairs of the interview after its first question: for each later question, the answer given just before it, and the question.

Reply with JSON only: an object with one key, "questions", a list with exactly one entry for every pair, in the same order. Each entry has "id", the question's id, and "follow_up", true or false.

Q2
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: That's fine, let's take it smaller. On your most recent shift, what was the very first thing you did when you sat down to work?

Q3
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: No problem. In your own words, what does your job as a dispatcher involve?

Q4
The answer just before it: As a dispatcher, I am the licensed person responsible for each flight, meaning I decide which drone flies and along which way, and I sign off a flight before it leaves. I can also call off a flight. Several dispatchers plan at the same time, often for the same busy sites and popular drones, and while software never picks a drone or a way for us, we do want help finding out which of our drones could get to where a job starts.
The question: Think of the last flight you signed off. What did you look at or check before you gave that sign-off?

Q9
The answer just before it: I worry about closures coming into force while our drones are already in the air, especially since zones and sudden closures can be announced or amended during the day. Radio coverage is patchy around ports, industrial sites, and in bad weather, and relay station reports can arrive late, out of order, more than once, or not at all. Batteries also drain faster in cold and wind than planned, and the service itself runs on a single server that is updated and restarted during working hours and occasionally crashes.
The question: When a closure comes into force while one of your drones is already in the air, what do you do today?

Q15
The answer just before it: I worry about instruction links to drones and charging equipment being unreliable, where an instruction might get through twice and the sender cannot tell if the first attempt arrived. I also worry about radio coverage being patchy around ports, industrial sites, and in bad weather, causing reports from drones to arrive late, out of order, more than once, or not at all. Additionally, it worries me that the service runs on a single server that is updated and restarted during working hours and occasionally crashes, accepting a few minutes of interruption.
The question: What worries you about the server restarting or crashing while you are in the middle of planning or have flights in the air?

The question: When the service comes back after one of those interruptions, what do you need to find when you look at it again?
